text_blocks.snippet: While there is no cancer that is 100% curable in all cases, some cancers have very high cure rates, especially when detected early. These include certain skin cancers (like basal cell and squamous cell), thyroid cancer, testicular cancer, and early-stage breast and prostate cancers. Cervical cancer, when detected early through routine screening, also has a high chance of recovery.
snippet_highlighted_words: skin cancers (like basal cell and squamous cell), thyroid cancer, testicular cancer, and early-stage breast and prostate cancers

list.snippet: Skin Cancer (Basal and Squamous Cell): When detected early, these cancers are highly curable.
Thyroid Cancer: Has a very high five-year survival rate, often exceeding 98%.
Testicular Cancer: Generally very curable, with over 95% of patients surviving five years or more when detected early.
Prostate Cancer: Has a very high five-year survival rate, especially when detected early through screening.
Cervical Cancer: When localized through screening, cervical cancer has a high chance of recovery.
Early-Stage Breast Cancer: The five-year survival rate is very high for Stage 0 and Stage I breast cancer.

related_questions.question: What cancer has the lowest survival rate?

text_blocks.snippet: Pancreatic cancer generally has the lowest five-year survival rate among common cancers. This is largely due to late-stage diagnosis and the cancer's resistance to many treatments, according to UnityPoint Health.
Here's why pancreatic cancer has such a low survival rate:

list.title: Late Stage Diagnosis:
list.snippet: Pancreatic cancer often doesn't cause noticeable symptoms in its early stages, leading to diagnosis at more advanced stages when it's harder to treat.

list.title: Rapid Progression:
list.snippet: The cancer tends to grow and spread quickly, making it difficult to control.

list.title: Treatment Resistance:
list.snippet: Pancreatic cancer has shown resistance to many standard cancer treatments, including chemotherapy.

list.title: Limited Early Detection Methods:
list.snippet: There are currently no widely effective methods for detecting pancreatic cancer in its early stages, which is crucial for successful treatment.
